text: Santokben Jadeja was a criminal and politician from Gujarat, popularly known as Godmother. She operated primarily in and around Porbandar and was a key figure in the region's criminal activities. Hailing from Kutiyana town in the Porbandar district, she served as a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from Kutiyana from 1990 to 1995 on a Janata Dal ticket and was closely associated with Chimanbhai Patel. Initially, until 1986, she lived a life as a homemaker and mother. Her husband, Sarman Munja Jadeja, an ordinary mill worker at Maharana Mill, became a gangster after killing Devu Vagher, who had been hired by the mill owner to break a strike. In December 1986, Sarman was killed by the Kala Keshav gang due to longstanding rivalry, which prompted Santokben to return to her husband's criminal ways to seek revenge. She was alleged to have orchestrated the murder of 14 individuals believed to be responsible for her husband's death. Her gang was reportedly composed of about 100 men, mostly from the Mer community, and during its peak in the late 1980s and early 1990s, it faced 525 criminal cases. She was booked in numerous murder cases, including the 2005 killing of Keshu Odedara, a Porbandar municipality councilor. In 2007, she was linked to the murder of Navghan Arsi, the son of Arsi Jadeja, her brother-in-law. In 2008, her daughter-in-law was shot dead by her son, Karan Jadeja. She was also arrested for providing shelter to individuals who raped two girls. In December 2002, she filed for nomination from Kutiyana but withdrew in favor of the Indian National Congress candidate. Her criminal operations spanned the 1980s and lasted about a decade, ending when she relocated to Rajkot. She died of a heart attack in Porbandar, Gujarat, on 31 March 2011. She was the subject of the Hindi film *Godmother* (1999), in which her role was portrayed by Shabana Azmi, who won the National Film Award for Best Actress; however, Santokben was not satisfied with the film's depiction of her.
